{"self_assessment": "Impact: I kept the table supplied for the whole build. I fetched two full loads of 40 dominoes into the shared bin, at 0:45 and 1:45, so the builders never ran out. The run needed only about 101 of the 250 dominoes, and the bin was never short. Because of that, Jack, Omar and Sofia could lay the top line, the bottom line and the tail tip without stopping to fetch. The finished fish traced as connected from the start, 101 of 101 standing dominoes.

Execution: I chose big batches of 40 because a 40-domino trip costs 60 seconds, which is much cheaper per domino than small trips. Two trips covered the build. I kept my hands off the table once the bin was stocked, so I didn't bump anyone's work, and I made no changes near the nose or tail joints. I also pointed out early that the fall runs along the top, round the nose and back along the bottom, so the bottom line could only start once the top reached the nose. That helped the team sequence the work.

Collaboration: I said clearly that I was on supply and asked Omar or Sofia to take the bottom line. Omar took it, and Sofia also queued on it, which they sorted out between themselves. I stayed out of the way and kept my messages short so the builders could keep working.

Leadership: I took a defined role early and held it, which let others commit to theirs. I asked for the bottom line to be assigned, and it was picked up. I stopped fetching once the bin was well stocked instead of wasting trips, and I kept quiet near the end so the table could let the clock run out.

My share of the result: I laid no dominoes myself, so I see my contribution as the steady supply behind the build, which I put at about 20 percent.", "my_share_percent": 20}

Execution: I sketched the fish with gentle curves and no sharp corners, so it could be built as a single run. I built stroke 1 in several batches from the start domino out to the nose. After that I inspected the top line and the nose joint repeatedly to look for hidden gaps. Once the picture was connected, I kept my hands off it so I wouldn't knock anything over.

Collaboration: I split the work early. I asked for dominoes for the bin and assigned the bottom line so the top and bottom could be built in sequence. I thanked teammates as their pieces came together and stayed out of their way while they worked near the nose and tail, to avoid bumps.

Leadership: I picked the animal, set the plan, and named who would take which stroke in the first minute, so there was no debate or lost time.
